caption: On a checkered world that never ended
Red raced the sunrise every morning.
Blue counted clouds that never came.
Red showed off. Blue pretended not to look.
Then White dropped in and called it a race.
First to the far edge wins, laughed White.
They ran until the ground hummed.
Then the ground stopped humming.
Then the Void opened one eye.
It took White mid laugh.
Red and Blue froze.
Red charged straight at Nothing.
And climbed right on top of it.
The Void wobbled.
It popped like a soap bubble.
Silence. Then footsteps.
White hopped back, dusty but grinning.
You rode it, gasped Blue.
Far away, the Void blinked.
They did not run this time.
They walked right past it.
And it shrank from being ignored.
No more races, said White.
Just the checkered world. And us.
